sections.title: The Ashes of Supermassive Stars: Globular Cluster-like Aluminum Enhancement in Little Red Dots
sections.abstract: JWST/SPURS spectroscopy finds magnesium-depleted, aluminum-enhanced gas at about 1% solar metallicity in Little Red Dots, a pattern the authors argue is reproduced by hot hydrogen burning in fully convective supermassive stars with masses of at least 10,000 solar masses.
sections.claimed_result: The observed abundance pattern is argued to be consistent with supermassive stars that could seed massive black holes.
sections.caveat: The interpretation is model-dependent and requires independent observations and modeling.

sections.title: A Spectral Framework for Testing the Quasi-Star Hypothesis in Little Red Dots I: Weighing LRDs by Their Super-Eddington Luminosity Ratios—No Signs of Overmassive Black Holes
sections.abstract: Atmosphere and envelope modeling of four absorption-rich Little Red Dots, extended to 82 archival objects, yields super-Eddington photospheres, envelope masses of 700–27,000 solar masses, and a self-consistent quasi-star interpretation.
sections.claimed_result: LRD central engines are argued to be compatible with black holes growing inside stellar-like envelopes.
sections.caveat: The largest inferred Eddington ratio lies beyond the simulation grid and mass estimates depend on model assumptions.

sections.title: Overmassive No More: The Case for Little Red Dots Hosting Black Hole Seeds as Massive as Single Supermassive Stars
sections.abstract: Tailored stellar-atmosphere fits to stacks of 117 Little Red Dots give pseudo-photospheres, inferred central masses of roughly 10^4–10^5 solar masses, and a possible interpretation as newly forming heavy black-hole seeds.
sections.claimed_result: Four mass-estimation approaches are argued to converge on a heavy-seed interpretation rather than overmassive black holes.
sections.caveat: The result depends on pseudo-photosphere, outflow, and dynamical assumptions.

sections.title: Private communication via zero-private-capacity quantum channels
sections.abstract: Two quantum channels, each with zero private capacity, are shown to jointly transmit more than 0.0001903 private bits per product use.
sections.claimed_result: The construction resolves a superactivation question in private quantum communication.
sections.caveat: The demonstrated rate is small and practical robustness remains open.

sections.title: Bell tests for collider decay processes
sections.abstract: The paper proposes collider Bell tests, identifies a postselection loophole, and derives conditions under which singlet correlations violate a Bell inequality.
sections.claimed_result: A suitable violation would witness Bell nonlocality or measurement contextuality under stated assumptions.
sections.caveat: No collider observation is reported; acceptance and analyzing power are key constraints.

sections.title: Two-magnon response from light scattering in altermagnets
sections.abstract: Spin-wave calculations predict momentum- and polarization-resolved two-magnon signatures of altermagnetism, including exchange-anisotropy-dependent spectral shifts and split resonances.
sections.claimed_result: Finite-momentum two-magnon spectroscopy is proposed as a route to identify altermagnetic order.
sections.caveat: The predictions use an idealized two-dimensional model and require material-specific validation.

sections.title: Nucleon Stron-Interactions Size From Charmonium Photoproduction
sections.abstract: Near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction and quark-sector information are combined to infer a nucleon strong-interaction spatial extent of 0.94 ± 0.09 fm.
sections.claimed_result: The extracted color-field distribution is reported to extend beyond electromagnetic charge and mass distributions.
sections.caveat: The extraction is model- and fit-dependent rather than a direct imaging measurement.
